original_batch.notes: Yamamoto-first discovery pass under the current durable repository authority. docs/PRIORITIES.md, docs/EDITORIAL.md, docs/DOMAINS.md, radar/inbox/README.md, and docs/DATA_MODEL.md were read before research or grading. Fresh Yamamoto research covered Jazz House ALFIE, BODY&SOUL, current Tsuyoshi Yamamoto schedule traces, Space M&A, and credible Japanese-jazz sources; the future Yamamoto appearances surfaced were already represented in canonical/curated/processed intake, so no duplicate Yamamoto record was created. Repository searches for Laraaji + National Sawdust + 2026-11-14, Numero Group + National Sawdust, The Album Leaf + 2026-11-14, and the proposed stable ID returned no existing RADAR match. Stage 1 admits the Numero Group 23rd Anniversary Celebration because the specific one-night bill is an explicit live cross-section of Numero's archival catalog: Laraaji, The Album Leaf, and Shira Small connect three very different strands of rediscovered or recontextualized music through the label's recovery work. This is a concrete curatorial, cultural-context and repertoire reason rather than venue prestige or name recognition. Stage 2 assigns A+. The unusual one-night bill is worth actively making room for if New York is in play. The scarcity challenge does not support S: the 23rd anniversary is not a singular historical milestone, the sources do not identify a farewell, final performance, premiere or last-ever configuration, and A+ fully captures the recommendation without inventing irreproducibility. Same-day and recent intake is already weighted toward A and A+ with scarcity tiers treated as rare, so this candidate adds no S/S+ pressure and remains consistent with the current rubric.

events.category: Archival-label anniversary / ambient / post-rock / outsider folk soul
events.factual_description: National Sawdust's current event page and current performances calendar list Murmrr Presents Numero Group — 23rd Anniversary Celebration on Saturday, November 14, 2026 at 7:30 PM, with doors at 6:30 PM, as an all-ages standing-room performance at 80 North 6th Street in Brooklyn. The announced bill is Laraaji, The Album Leaf, and Shira Small. National Sawdust describes the event as a night of live music spanning the Numero-verse catalog held to commemorate Numero Group's 23rd anniversary while the label is closing out its New York pop-up period. The individual event page contains a stale 'This event has passed' label, but the venue's current performances page lists the November 14 event among upcoming performances and the authorized AudienceView/OvationTix ticket destination remains active; the current calendar and active ticket route therefore control status. Numero Group identifies itself as an archival label founded in 2003 and documents direct catalog/reissue relationships with Laraaji, The Album Leaf, and Shira Small. No event-specific instruments, backing personnel, set order, ticket price, or special collaborations are stated in the checked sources, so none are inferred.

en.why_it_matters: Numero turns its archival instinct into a live, one-night cross-section of the catalog: Laraaji's devotional ambient world, The Album Leaf's post-rock/electronic language, and Shira Small's rediscovered 1970s songwriting share a bill that only really makes sense through the label's recovery work. The draw is the curation itself — three different eras and forms of outsider music placed in conversation rather than three unrelated sets sharing a room.
en.trip_verdict: If New York is in play that weekend, actively make room for the November 14 gathering at National Sawdust; the unusual bill is the reason to choose this night over a routine club date. From the DMV, I would still pair it with another strong New York reason rather than reshape a broader East Coast trip around this event alone.
en.listen_before: Laraaji — Segue To Infinity; The Album Leaf — One Day I'll Be On Time; Shira Small — The Line of Time and the Plane of Now

es.why_it_matters: Numero convierte su instinto de archivo en una muestra viva del catálogo por una sola noche: el mundo ambient y devocional de Laraaji, el lenguaje post-rock/electrónico de The Album Leaf y las canciones setenteras recuperadas de Shira Small comparten un cartel que sólo termina de tener sentido por el trabajo de rescate del sello. Lo atractivo es la curaduría misma: tres épocas y tres formas distintas de música fuera del centro puestas a conversar, no tres sets inconexos compartiendo sala.
es.trip_verdict: Si Nueva York ya está en juego ese fin de semana, le haría espacio activamente a la reunión del 14 de noviembre en National Sawdust; el cartel poco común es la razón para elegir esa noche sobre una fecha rutinaria de club. Desde el DMV, aun así lo combinaría con otra razón fuerte para subir a Nueva York en vez de rehacer un viaje regional completo alrededor de este concierto.
